comments.author: @Jo_Wick
comments.text:
I'm going to be honest: I heard the news and was very excited to try out the new Gemini 3 I had been hearing about for the last few months. When I did, it took me one question I spontaneously thought of for it to make two stunningly obvious math errors regarding a hypothetical partitioning of a flash device. They weren't in-the-weeds math questions, either: It was a simple "So because partitioning an SD card into two equal parts (50% of the space), the "loop" completes 50% faster." The "loop" it refers to is essentially the ring-around-the-rosie selection of logical sectors to use for read-write cycles. With that statement, it essentially contradicted itself from earlier, when it said "The controller now has to perform garbage collection and erase cycles twice as often on that specific subset of logical blocks to keep up with the incoming video stream."

The correct answer was 2x (100% faster). I'm not a math major, but that immediately made me feel like Gemini 3 wasn't a real improvement, generally speaking.


The other math error it made was because it was "guesstimating," so not a true math error, but it was a pretty bad estimation if I've seen one. It was talking about high-endurance flash memory, and it said:
"They might take a 64 GiB raw chip but market it as only 50 GB or 52 GB... This leaves roughly 28% of the raw flash accessible only to the controller"

I took one look at "28%" and I was like, "that's not even 25%." When you run the numbers, my intuition was proven correct... the true percent is only 23% when rounded to the nearest percent.

Update: I sent my prompt to anonymous-user chatGPT and Claude 4.5 Sonnet; neither of them got this kind of math wrong, but they also didn't mention these numbers at all. They just all agreed that it was a bad idea to partition it, though I will say Gemini was the most thorough in explaining why.

This does not feel like a smarter model, at least generally speaking. It may do better in some narrow tasks, but it's still prone to hallucinations like the rest of them. Speaking of hallucination rates... Anyone know the benchmarks on that? I'm also wondering if my use of Gemini 3 on the gemini web interface played a role (I selected the thinking option).
